title: Smallest Divisible Digit Product II
summary: Given a string representing a positive integer and an integer t, find the smallest zero-free number greater than or equal to the input number where the product of its digits is divisible by t.
statement: Given a string representing a positive integer and an integer t, find the smallest zero-free number greater than or equal to the input number where the product of its digits is divisible by t. If no such number exists, return "-1".
constraints: num has 2–200,000 digits with no leading zero; 1 <= t <= 100,000,000,000,000.
Return the smallest zero-free decimal number at least num whose digit product is divisible by t.
Return -1 only when t contains a prime factor other than 2, 3, 5, or 7.
hints: A decimal digit contributes only prime factors 2,3,5,7; any other required prime makes the task impossible.
Preserve the longest feasible prefix, increase its rightmost possible digit, then fill the suffix with the smallest factor-covering digits.
Track residual prime exponents across the prefix; test larger digits right-to-left; pack remaining 2/3 exponents optimally and append required 5/7 digits after leading ones.
The rightmost feasible increase minimizes the fixed-length result, and the shortest sorted factor multiset maximizes leading ones in its suffix.
editorial: The rightmost feasible increase minimizes the fixed-length result, and the shortest sorted factor multiset maximizes leading ones in its suffix.

tests.explanation: Keeping prefix 1, increasing 2 to 4, and using suffix 88 produces the minimum valid 1488.
The input is already zero-free and its digit product 150 is divisible by 50.
